stories.headline: FED HOLDS RATES BUT DOTS FLIP TO A HIKE IN WARSH'S DEBUT
stories.body: The FOMC voted 12-0 to keep the funds rate at 3.5%-3.75% in Kevin Warsh's first meeting as chair, but the median dot for end-2026 jumped to 3.8% from 3.4% in March, with 9 of 18 officials now penciling in at least one hike. Money markets quickly moved to fully price a hike by October.
stories.explain: The dot plot, not the rate itself, drove the session: shifting the median projection up 40 bps tells investors the next move is up, not down. That lifts the discount rate on future cash flows, which is why long-duration megacap tech — Meta, Microsoft, Amazon — led the decline. Warsh's 'price stability' framing and a curt new statement reinforced the hawkish reset.

stories.headline: STOCKS PLUNGE AS HAWKISH FED REPRICING HITS MEGACAP TECH
stories.body: The S&P 500 fell 1.21% to 7,420.10 and the Nasdaq-100 dropped roughly 1.3% as every sector finished lower. Communication services led losses down 2.91% and consumer cyclicals fell 2.34%. The Dow shed 0.98% to 51,492.55.
stories.explain: When the Fed signals higher-for-longer, the hit lands hardest on the most rate-sensitive, highest-multiple names, whose valuations lean on cash flows far in the future. With the 10-year jumping to 4.49%, the equity risk premium compressed and traders rotated out of crowded AI winners — though ASML rose 4% and Broadcom gained on chip-spending optimism, a reminder the selloff was about rates, not earnings.

stories.headline: OIL SLIDES TO MARCH LOWS ON IMMINENT US-IRAN DEAL
stories.body: WTI crude fell about 1.6% toward $75 a barrel, its weakest level since early March, as traders positioned for a US-Iran interim agreement expected to be signed Friday that could quickly return Iranian barrels to global supply.
stories.explain: Oil trades on the marginal barrel, and a deal easing sanctions plus restrictions through the Strait of Hormuz would add supply into a market already adequately stocked. The prospect pulls the geopolitical risk premium out of crude — notably, oil's drop was a supply story that ran independent of the Fed-driven risk-off in equities and metals on the same day.

stories.headline: GOLD DROPS 1.8% AS HIGHER RATES AND A FIRMER DOLLAR BITE
stories.body: Gold fell about 1.8% to roughly $4,255 an ounce after the Fed decision, paring a weekly gain. The dollar index firmed to 99.65 and the 10-year yield rose six basis points to 4.49%.
stories.explain: Gold pays no yield, so its opportunity cost rises whenever real rates and the dollar climb — exactly what a hawkish dot plot delivers. The metal had rallied earlier in the week on demand for a hedge ahead of the US-Iran signing, but the Fed's higher-for-longer signal overwhelmed that bid, illustrating how monetary policy can trump geopolitics for non-yielding assets.

stories.headline: PORTAL RESHUFFLES BLUEBLOODS AS DRAFT DECISIONS FIRM UP
stories.body: Iowa State sharpshooter Milan Momcilovic (48.7% from three, 16.9 ppg) withdrew from the NBA Draft and committed to Kentucky, while Wake Forest's Juke Harris (21.4 ppg) picked Tennessee and 7-2 center Moustapha Thiam chose Michigan. Kansas's Jalen Bidunga declared for the June 25 draft while keeping eligibility.

stories.headline: KNICKS WIN FIRST TITLE SINCE 1973; DRAFT LOOMS JUNE 23
stories.body: The New York Knicks closed out Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs 94-90 in Game 5 to win the Finals 4-1, capping a 13-game postseason run and earning Jalen Brunson Finals MVP. Attention turns to the 2026 NBA Draft, which opens June 23.

stories.headline: MINICAMPS WIND DOWN WITH QB HEALTH IN FOCUS
stories.body: Falcons QB Michael Penix Jr. (knee) remained limited and not cleared for 11-on-11 work, while Titans rookie Cam Ward said his surgically repaired throwing shoulder is fine. Eight teams, including the Cowboys and Falcons, wrap mandatory minicamp June 18 before summer break.

stories.headline: TRANSFER PORTAL CLASSES SET AS QUIET PERIOD BEGINS
stories.body: With the portal effectively closed, Penn State's new staff imported nearly 40 transfers led by QB Rocco Becht, Texas Tech landed top dual-threat QB Brendan Sorsby, and LSU built the No. 1-ranked class under Lane Kiffin. Coaches opened direct contact with 2028 recruits on June 15.

deepDive.title: The Dot Plot Flips: How a 40-Basis-Point Projection Reset Roiled Markets
content: The Fed left its policy rate untouched on Wednesday, yet stocks fell more than a percent. That apparent paradox is the whole lesson of the day. In Kevin Warsh's first meeting as chair, the FOMC held the funds rate at 3.5%-3.75% exactly as a 97% chance had implied. What moved markets sat in the Summary of Economic Projections: the median dot for end-2026 climbed to 3.8% from 3.4% in March. Nine of eighteen officials now see at least one hike this year, six see two or more, and money markets responded by fully pricing a hike by October.

The dot plot is the Fed's collective forecast of where the funds rate is headed, and it functions as forward guidance that markets discount immediately. Equity valuations are present values of future cash flows; raise the rate those flows are discounted at, even on paper, and prices fall — most for the longest-duration assets. That is precisely why communication services dropped 2.91% and megacap tech like Meta, Microsoft and Amazon led losses while the S&P 500 shed 1.21% to 7,420. The 10-year yield rose six basis points to 4.49%, the dollar firmed to 99.65, and gold fell 1.8%.

What makes this notable is the direction of the revision. For most of the post-2022 era, dot-plot adjustments debated how fast to cut. A median that shifts toward hikes is a regime signal, not a tweak — the kind of pivot last seen when inflation surprised to the upside. Warsh, long viewed as hawkish, leaned in, repeatedly invoking 'price stability' and unveiling a deliberately 'curt' statement plus five task forces to overhaul Fed operations. Markets read the stylistic break as substantive: a new chair willing to tolerate a higher rate path to defend the inflation mandate, even at the cost of a sharp equity wobble.

The practical upshot is a higher-for-longer rate environment with the tail risk now skewed toward tightening rather than easing. For investors, that compresses equity multiples, supports the dollar, and pressures non-yielding assets like gold whose opportunity cost rises with real rates. Notably, oil decoupled, sliding to March lows on an imminent US-Iran deal — a reminder that supply shocks and monetary policy can pull in opposite directions on the same day. The signal to watch is the October meeting: if incoming inflation data validates the dots, Warsh's first projection reset becomes the opening move of a genuine hiking cycle.
